item.title: Commercial bins causing foul smell and pest issues outside business windows, 26th August
item.description:
Dear Greenwich council team ​I am writing to report a severe public health and safety issue regarding commercial waste bins that are permanently left standing directly outside our ground floor premises at unit 2 10 little thames walk london se8 3fb ​These large industrial bins are not just brought out for collection they are left here permanently five days a week or even longer right next to our side doors and front windows where we operate a tattoo studio and a barber shop the situation has become completely unacceptable for our business and public health for several reasons. ​Firstly the permanent presence of these bins is attracting rats and mice posing a serious health hazard to us and our clients. Secondly the rotting waste produces a strong foul odor that spreads directly into our studio and shop whenever doors or windows are open. Thirdly customers arriving at our business are immediately greeted by these overflowing containers and complain about the terrible conditions right at our entrance ​this is causing major damage to our business reputation and creating an unsafe working environment these bins must be permanently removed from this location and stored elsewhere away from commercial shopfronts and pedestrian paths. ​Please investigate this matter urgently and take enforcement action to ensure these bins are no longer stored in this public area ​

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Little Thames Walk, Deptford
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Nw3 7sn, 26th August
item.description:
I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the repeated unsafe and inappropriate parking of hire e-bikes at and around 8A Heath Drive, London NW3 7SN. This has become a persistent problem for residents. I have photographic evidence of numerous Forest and other dockless hire bikes being left around the building in positions that obstruct driveways, interfere with vehicle access, create trip hazards and place residents’ cars at risk. Your own guidance states that Camden is a mandatory parking-bay borough. Your guidance also states that users should find another location if a parking bay is full and should leave sufficient space for pedestrians, wheelchair users and pushchairs. The repeated behaviour at our building is therefore particularly concerning.The repeated behaviour at our building is therefore particularly concerning. The problems include: Bikes being left across or immediately adjacent to residents’ driveways , pedestrian walkways etc. Bikes being left lying down or in unstable positions. Bikes being left against residents’ vehicles. Bikes falling onto vehicles. Residents having to move heavy bikes themselves. Repeated accumulation of bikes in the same residential location when clearly There is no space . Camden needs to act on this and enforce their rules as innocent residents are suffering and my car parked in resident bay hit by bikes. we are fed up. Camden council Need to access weather or not this location is indeed appropriate for these bikes and do Something about it

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Heath Drive, West Hampstead, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
